title.en: NBI source-plane ray with aperture acceptance

summary: Map caller-provided uniform source samples and standard-normal divergence samples into the FIDASIM beam-coordinate source point and unit ray, then accept the ray only if it passes every rectangular or elliptical aperture.

identity.relation: rectangle source: xyz_source = [0, hy*2*(u0-0.5), hz*2*(u1-0.5)]; ellipse source: xyz_source = [0, hy*sqrt(u0)*cos(2*pi*u1), hz*sqrt(u0)*sin(2*pi*u1)]; xyz_ray = [1, -y_src/focy + tan(divy*n0), -z_src/focz + tan(divz*n1)]; per aperture at point = xyz_ray*d + xyz_source: rectangle (shape=1) or ellipse (shape=2) closed acceptance test; source_beam = basis @ xyz_source + origin; unit_ray = normalize(basis @ xyz_ray).
identity.direction: source uniform/normal variates + source shape/half-widths + focus lengths + divergences + aperture set + beam basis/origin -> source point, unit ray, acceptance flag
identity.definition: The saved FIDASIM mc_nbi source-plane branch (framework node N2 neutral_beam_source_sampling): the deterministic geometry between caller random variates and the aperture-accepted beam-coordinate ray. Randomness is caller-owned; the 1000-attempt rejection loop and the serial two-word RNG are runtime sampling mechanics outside this relation.
identity.model: the saved formal implementation, ported verbatim with registered finite/norm hardenings
identity.geometry: one NBI source plane with lateral focusing and divergence, projected through an ordered aperture set into beam coordinates
identity.coordinates: positions in cm; angles and divergences in radians; the beam basis maps xyz to beam-grid uvw; outputs are dimensionless unit rays
identity.boundary: uniform samples exactly in [0,1]; finite shape-(2,) variate pairs; source_shape exactly 1 or 2 (bools rejected); positive finite half-widths; nonzero finite focus lengths; finite divergence standard deviations; finite (3,3) basis and (3,) origin; aligned finite aperture vectors; the transformed ray norm must stay finite and nonzero; all outputs finite
assumptions: The caller supplies a geometrically consistent beam basis, source geometry and aperture set.
Rejection resampling, the 1000-attempt cap and the source serial RNG remain caller-owned runtime mechanics.

inputs.name: source_shape
inputs.constraints: Exactly 1 or 2 (registered: Python and NumPy bools rejected).

inputs.name: divergence_y_rad
inputs.constraints: Finite (registered: the saved arm propagates NaN silently).

inputs.name: divergence_z_rad
inputs.constraints: Finite (registered: the saved arm propagates NaN silently).

inputs.name: aperture_distance_cm
inputs.constraints: Finite; same length as the other aperture vectors.

inputs.name: beam_basis
inputs.constraints: Finite; transformed ray norm must stay finite and nonzero.

outputs.name: source_beam_cm
outputs.description: Source point in beam coordinates: basis @ xyz_source + origin.

outputs.name: unit_ray_beam
outputs.description: Normalized basis @ xyz_ray in beam coordinates.
outputs.constraints: Finite; unit norm (registered: an overflowing squared norm raises instead of collapsing to a zero vector).

outputs.name: accepted
outputs.description: Whether the ray passes every aperture.

preconditions: A geometrically consistent beam basis, source geometry and aperture set.
supported: Per-event deterministic NBI source-plane ray geometry, aperture acceptance and beam-coordinate projection.
excluded: Random-variates generation, rejection resampling loops, cell-targeted sampling, trajectory following and ionization physics.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when any variate pair, geometry vector, basis, origin or aperture entry is non-finite or misshaped, when uniform samples leave [0,1], when source_shape is not exactly 1 or 2 (including Python and NumPy bools), when a half-width is non-positive, when a focus length is zero or non-finite, when a divergence is non-finite, or when aperture_shape values are not 1 or 2.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the transformed ray norm is non-finite or zero, or when any output is non-finite, for finite but extreme input magnitudes (registered hardening); the saved arm silently returns a collapsed zero 'unit' ray or NaN geometry.

example.description: The saved package's centerline probe: a centered rectangle sample maps to the beam origin and the unit centerline passes the aperture.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.fusion import construct_nbi_source_ray
source, ray, accepted = construct_nbi_source_ray(
    [0.5, 0.5], [0.0, 0.0], 1, 2.0, 3.0, 10.0, 10.0, 0.1, 0.1,
    [5.0], [1], [0.0], [0.0], [1.0], [1.0], np.eye(3), [1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
assert np.allclose(source, [1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
assert np.allclose(ray, [1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
assert accepted
try:
    construct_nbi_source_ray(
        [1, 0.5], [0, 0], 1, 1e200, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0,
        [], [], [], [], [], [], np.eye(3), np.zeros(3))
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('an overflowing ray norm must be rejected (registered hardening)')
example.expected: The centerline probe reproduces the saved mapping; the extreme-geometry call that collapses the saved arm's unit ray to a zero vector raises ValueError.

scope: Saved-package probe reproduction (centerline rectangle acceptance and beam-coordinate mapping).
Closed-form rectangle/ellipse source mappings, focus and divergence ray terms, aperture acceptance bounds.
Registered hardenings: finite focus/divergence/half-widths, Python- and NumPy-bool source-shape rejection, finite-and-nonzero ray norm, finite outputs.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct tests reproduce the saved package's own centerline probe, recompute the rectangle/ellipse source mappings and the ray focusing/divergence terms in closed form, verify the beam-basis transform identity, and exercise the aperture acceptance bounds plus the fail-closed contracts including the norm-overflow gate added after independent pre-freeze review. The aperture test is closed-form geometry; no source MC replay, rejection-loop or whole-source composition is asserted. The saved FIDASIM packages ship package-level oracles rather than a pinned source-runtime replay target, and the recorded implementation digest provides the provenance linkage. No test establishes the relation against an external physics reference beyond the source closed form.
